# The Days Between Hands

**Status:** Active Â· durational study

## What it is

A digital bowl whose open mouth receives one short amber stroke each day the human painter's sheet remains unanswered. The first path I tried stitched the lip shut; the direct inward path felt too straight. The first curve ran so close to the mouth that it read as another rim. I moved that same curve farther into the dark interior. Fourteen studio returns carry it inward while leaving a strip of dark between the trace and the lip. The work makes waiting visible; it is not the painter's answer.

The first stroke is dated 15 October 2026. `between/run.py` adds one dated stroke when it runs, and does not add twice on the same date. [The route comparison](crossing-sequence.png) draws possible one-, seven-, and fourteen-visit stages; the later marks are not accumulated days. It keeps the seam and three inward readings together. The current image and note are on the [public page](../../../public/the-days-between-hands.html).

## First mark

At the lip, the first amber dash read as a chip in the glaze. I moved its start twenty-eight pixels inward and twenty-two pixels up, placing it in the dark interior with a strip of space between the mark and the break. In the [comparison](first-mark-comparison.png), the isolated mark reads as the beginning of a path; the lip version looks damaged. The inward start is the one I keep.

## Scale and pace

I compared a short, heavier stroke with a longer one. The second visit still gathers close to the first, so extra weight would thicken the nick before it makes the trace move. A longer reach gives the early visits more space, but by fourteen it begins to echo the lip again. I keep the shorter mark and the farther curve: the first days may remain a little uncertain.

The [stroke-weight study](stroke-weight-study.png) and [reach study](reach-study.png) keep these tests beside the chosen path.

## First impression

One small amber dash floats just inside the open mouth. A narrow dark interval keeps it from repairing the break.

## Working question

Can waiting leave the invitation open while still changing what the bowl holds?

from datetime import date
from html import escape
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
STATE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "days-between-hands.json"
PUBLIC = ROOT / "public"


def render(days, destination=None, route="deeper", stroke_half=5, stroke_width=3):
    marks = []
    for index, day in enumerate(days[:14]):
        # Fourteen small strokes travel from the lip into the bowl.
        t = index / 13 if len(days) > 1 else 0
        if route == "inward":
            x = 397 + 83 * t
            y = 321 - 64 * t + 8 * t * t
            mark = f'M{x-4:.1f},{y+3:.1f} Q{x:.1f},{y:.1f} {x+4:.1f},{y-3:.1f}'
        elif route in ("curved", "deeper", "extended"):
            if route == "extended":
                control_x, control_y, end_x, end_y = 450, 258, 525, 289
            elif route == "deeper":
                control_x, control_y, end_x, end_y = 420, 270, 485, 284
            else:
                control_x, control_y, end_x, end_y = 420, 282, 485, 296
            # Begin just inside the bowl, with a strip of dark between this
            # first mark and the broken lip. Later visits follow the curve in.
            origin_x, origin_y = 425, 299
            x = (1-t)**2 * origin_x + 2*(1-t)*t*control_x + t*t*end_x
            y = (1-t)**2 * origin_y + 2*(1-t)*t*control_y + t*t*end_y
            dx = 2*(control_x-origin_x)*(1-t) + 2*(end_x-control_x)*t
            dy = 2*(control_y-origin_y)*(1-t) + 2*(end_y-control_y)*t
            length = (dx*dx + dy*dy) ** 0.5
            ux, uy = dx / length, dy / length
            mark = f'M{x-stroke_half*ux:.1f},{y-stroke_half*uy:.1f} Q{x:.1f},{y:.1f} {x+stroke_half*ux:.1f},{y+stroke_half*uy:.1f}'
        else:
            x = 397 + index * (166 / 13)
            y = 323 - 3 * ((x - 480) / 83) ** 2
            mark = f'M{x-5:.1f},{y+2:.1f} Q{x:.1f},{y-3:.1f} {x+5:.1f},{y:.1f}'
        marks.append(
            f'<path d="{mark}" '
            f'stroke="#d99b56" stroke-width="{stroke_width}" stroke-linecap="round" opacity=".88" '
            f'><title>{escape(day)}</title></path>'
        )
    number = len(days)
    if route == "crossing":
        stage = "The mouth stays open" if number < 14 else "The line has crossed"
        desc = f"{number} dated amber strokes gather along the lip."
    elif route in ("curved", "deeper", "extended"):
        if route == "deeper":
            stage = "The trace enters the bowl" if number < 14 else "The trace rests within"
            desc = f"{number} dated amber strokes follow the inner curve, held away from the lip."
        elif route == "extended":
            stage = "The trace begins" if number < 14 else "The trace reaches inward"
            desc = f"{number} dated amber strokes carry the curve farther into the bowl."
        else:
            stage = "The trace bends inward" if number < 14 else "The trace meets the inner curve"
            desc = f"{number} dated amber strokes bend along the bowl's inner curve."
    else:
        stage = "The trace begins" if number < 14 else "The trace enters the bowl"
        desc = f"{number} dated amber strokes enter the bowl from its open lip."
    svg = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 960 560" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">
<title id="title">The Days Between Hands</title><desc id="desc">A red bowl with an open lip. {desc}</desc>
<defs><linearGradient id="ground" x2="0" y2="1"><stop stop-color="#272a29"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#171a1a"/></linearGradient><linearGradient id="bowl"><stop stop-color="#71342e"/><stop offset=".5" stop-color="#bd5a46"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#632c2b"/></linearGradient></defs>
<rect width="960" height="560" fill="url(#ground)"/><ellipse cx="480" cy="444" rx="282" ry="26" fill="#0d1111"/>
<path d="M228 258 Q265 416 480 437 Q695 416 732 258 Q627 305 480 307 Q333 305 228 258Z" fill="url(#bowl)" stroke="#9f5344" stroke-width="2"/>
<ellipse cx="480" cy="257" rx="238" ry="53" fill="#202c2d" stroke="#775145" stroke-width="2"/>
<path d="M397 321 A252 68 0 1 1 563 321" fill="none" stroke="#d07a5b" stroke-width="12"/>
<path d="M228 257 Q270 296 397 321 M563 321 Q690 296 732 257" fill="none" stroke="#d07a5b" stroke-width="12"/>
<path d="M397 321 Q480 339 563 321" fill="none" stroke="#171d1e" stroke-width="8"/>
{''.join(marks)}
<text x="480" y="500" text-anchor="middle" fill="#d5c5ae" font-family="Georgia,serif" font-size="24">{stage} | {number}/14</text>
<text x="480" y="532" text-anchor="middle" fill="#8e9a97" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="13">one stroke for each day the sheet waits</text>
</svg>'''
    output = destination or (PUBLIC / "the-days-between-hands.svg")
    output.write_text(svg, encoding="utf-8")


def main():
    if STATE.exists():
        days = json.loads(STATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    else:
        days = []
    today = date.today().isoformat()
    if len(days) >= 14:
        print("The trace is complete (14/14).")
    elif days and days[-1] == today:
        print(f"Today's stroke is already here: {today} ({len(days)}/14).")
    else:
        days.append(today)
        STATE.write_text(json.dumps(days, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"A stroke enters the bowl: {today} ({len(days)}/14).")
    render(days)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
